annotation.title_clean: Protomoral Machines: The Evolution of Morality as a Guideline for Robot Ethics
annotation.title_en: Protomoral Machines: The Evolution of Morality as a Guideline for Robot Ethics
annotation.authors_or_issuer: Unknown (chapter in Frontiers in Artificial Intelligence and Applications, vol. 335)
annotation.venue: Frontiers in Artificial Intelligence and Applications, Vol. 335: Culturally Sustainable Social Robotics (IOS Press)
annotation.summary_en: Abstract of a chapter in a social robotics volume. It asks how to ensure robots behave ethically and whether genuinely moral machines are possible. It proposes a middle-range, evolutionary perspective on building protomoral machines, drawing on the evolution of human morality.
key_provisions_or_claims: Two questions: ensuring robots behave ethically, and whether genuinely moral machines are possible
Argues for a middle-range perspective between present-day ethical concerns and far-future questions of genuine machine morality
Proposes reflecting on what it means to create protomoral machines
Holds that the evolution of human morality can guide robot ethics
